annotations.title: Next of his blood.
annotations.text: [1] Marriage is forbid first and most strictly by the law of nature, in all degrees in the right line ascending and descending, both in consanguinity and affinity. S. Paul condemneth [2] (1 Cor. 5. v. 1.) even among the Pagans, the unlawful match of a son and mother. And in the right line God himself (who only can) never dispensed. [3] Secondarily, the first collateral degree in consanguinity, that is, between brother and sister, by one parent, or by both, is also unlawful by the law of nature, except in the beginning of the world, when Adam's children must needs marry together [4] but after this beginning it was never allowed [5], nor perhaps can be dispensed withal, at least never was by any man. Though Beza (li. de repudiis & divortiis) and some English Heretics call Pope Martin fift, to have dispensed with one, that had married his sister. [6] So this present law, written by Moyses, forbad to marry in the first collateral degree of affinity, but only positively. So the same law commanded (Deut. 25.) that in case a married man die without issue, his brother should marry the widow: which sheweth the degree was not of nature, but only positive. For then God would not have made a contrary general law in any case, for the whole nation of the Jews, his people; and that under penalty to be observed, which is contrary to the quality of indulgence or dispensation, and no such necessity, as in the beginning of the world. [7] [8] Whether degrees of consanguinity and affinity is the law of nature, and so pertaineth to Christians, must necessarily say also, that if now a married man die without issue, his brother must marry his wife. Which specially they deny. [9] It is also proved that this and some other degrees expressed in this place, were not against the law of nature (which is common to all men, or commonly known to all men by discourse of reason) [10] because no common-wealth among the Gentiles did punish, nor modest men forbear, or reprehend such marriages: as apparently by Laban, who gave or he had deceived Jacob (Gen. 29.) And because that which God's law promised, when Jacob had married with the wife of his first son, he did it according to the custom of that place & time & law. [11] And the law ruling at that time of the Synagogue commanded it (Deu. 25. 5. 20) neither did Jacob question the same at all with his first wife. And Judas matched his second son. And this same law forbiddeth a man to marry, or company with his wife's sister, it addeth, whiles she is living, not prohibiting marriage, when his first wife is dead. Yet his wife's sister is as near in affinity, as his brother's wife. [12] Likewise, the diversity of punishments (chap. 26) for transgressing in the first collateral degree of consanguinity, where the penalty was only by death; and for transgressing in the first collateral degree of affinity, or in the second either of consanguinity or affinity, who had less punishments, sheweth that the former degrees are prohibited by the law of nature, and not the other: or they were: some natural, some positive and punished alike. [13] Finally, it is evident, that certain of these degrees are not against the law of nature, by the example of Abraham, who in, and according to the law of nature, married his brother's daughter called Sara, otherwise Joscha, Gen 11. which marriage God approved many blessings. [14] Also two sisters together at the same time married to the same man successively. And Amram (Moyses' father) married his aunt, his father's sister, Exo 6. v. 20. Num 26. v. 59. Wherefore seeing neither the first collateral degree in affinity, nor the second collateral in consanguinity or affinity, is forbid by the law of nature but by positive only, and that both ceremonial & judicial laws of the old Testament ceased in the New, and are abrogated by Christ [15], it resteth proved that the same bind not Christians, but as they are renewed and established by the Church, or Christian common-wealths. And as this is done in temporal causes by temporal States, partly by renewing and establishing the same, which was in the law of Moyses, as by punishing wilful murder by death, Exo. 21. v. 12. partly with alteration, as by punishing theft in some countries with death, but not adultery, which were contrary in the old Testament, Gen. 38. v. 24. 44. 17. Exod. 22. v. 1. Levit. 20 v. 10. in like sort the Church of Christ ordaineth laws [16], altereth, & upon just occasions dispenseth, in all degrees of consanguinity and affinity, and doth not forbid by the law of nature.

notes.text: Marriage forbid in all degrees in the right line by the law of nature.
Secondarily, the first collateral degree of consanguinity.
S. Aug. l. 9. de Gen. ad lit.
Whether degrees depend on positive laws: which have been & may be altered. Proved by Scriptures, and reasons.
Christ abrogated the ceremonial and judicial laws of the old Testament.
The Church of Christ ordaineth laws, and upon just occasions dispenseth in all degrees of consanguinity and affinity.
